summary: Phase 149O.20L.7O.2L.1 is a code-implementation-only phase (no real Trust-Enrollment effect performed). It implemented exactly the two standalone Protected Admin scripts Phase 149O.20L.7O.2L's architecture re-derivation named as the sole missing artifact: scripts/hatp_hardware_credential_admin.py (subcommands enroll/recover/revoke, wrapping Fido2HardwareProvider.enroll_credential() plus pcae.core.hatp_hardware_credential_admin's register_credential/revoke_credential) and scripts/hatp_principal_signer_admin.py (subcommands enroll-principal/revoke-principal/enroll-signer/revoke-signer, wrapping pcae.core.hatp_principal_signer_admin's four writer operations). Both scripts are thin, fail-closed wrappers: administrative input parsing -> protected confirmation boundary -> call the existing core writer -> render a deterministic result. Neither reimplements record parsing, validation, identity derivation, locking, persistence, duplicate detection, revocation semantics, or DeploymentBinding cross-validation -- AST-walked import-graph analysis confirmed every module either script imports is already inside hatp_mandatory_certification.py's frozen v1.6 source set. The load-bearing design decision (governing prompt Section 9/10/27): enroll never accepts caller-supplied credential identity (always the live FIDO2 makeCredential ceremony's own output); the one deliberate exception is recover, which retries only the registry write using RECOVERY EVIDENCE enroll prints to stderr on a hardware-success-then-persistence-failure, safe by construction via the core writer's own _candidate_equal idempotency (retrying with identical evidence is a no-op if the original write actually landed and a genuine write if it did not; retrying with different evidence fails closed as a conflict) -- never re-touching the physical device, which would mint a second, distinct credential. enroll-signer's HPSE-REQ-056/HPSE-REQ-057/HHCE-REQ-037 continuous two-lock critical section is preserved intact as a single call into the unmodified core enroll_signer() function -- AST-verified exactly one call site, no manual lock acquisition anywhere in the script. A fresh HMIC-REQ-052 analysis was performed independently against current production hatp_mandatory_certification.py (not restated from 2L's own prose): both new scripts independently answer YES to 'could the protected Trust-Enrollment result change if only this script were modified while every currently-frozen v1.6 member stayed byte-identical' -- each is the sole, real, standalone administrative ceremony deciding which core-writer call happens, with what evidence, after what confirmation. Because both scripts' entire reachable import surface is already inside the frozen v1.6 set, the exact future HMIC-REQ-050 delta is derived precisely as +2 (36 -> 38), both entries belonging in _FROZEN_REPOSITORY_ROOT_RELATIVE_FILES (repository-root-relative, mirroring the two other Protected Admin scripts' own existing binding precedent) -- no HMIC-001 amendment performed in this phase. 88 new focused tests were added: 29 in tests/test_hatp_hardware_credential_admin_script.py (--help, argument validation, declined confirmation, --preview, synthetic-FIDO2 success, hardware-success-then-persistence-failure recovery evidence, safe recover retry in both landed/never-landed cases, conflicting retry, no duplicate record, malformed store, revoke success/idempotent/not-found/preview, no secret output, no store-root override), 31 in tests/test_hatp_principal_signer_admin_script.py (--help, argument validation, declined confirmation, missing hardware-credential precondition, missing/revoked principal, provider-profile mismatch, successful enroll/revoke for both principal and signer, idempotent replay, conflicting existing principal/signer, revoked hardware credential, malformed store, no secret output, no DeploymentBinding created, no HMIC import), and 28 in tests/test_phase_149o_20l_7o_2l_1_hatp_trust_enrollment_admin_entrypoint_implementation.py (contract-text-unchanged, core-writer-unchanged since phase entry, AST-verified import-surface closure, no-reimplemented-locking/persistence, continuous-two-lock-preserved via AST single-call-site verification, no-caller-supplied-credential-identity-on-enroll, fresh HMIC-REQ-052 analysis assertions, no secret CLI flags). All 88 pass. Three pre-existing phase-boundary test assertions were found to be superseded by this phase's own implementation (each had asserted, truthfully at its own phase's entry state, that the two scripts did not yet exist) and were updated in place, documenting the supersession rather than silently deleting the historical record: tests/test_phase_149o_20l_7o_2l_post_hmic_activation_trust_enrollment_dag.py, tests/test_phase_149o_20l_7o_2h_3_hmic_paths_source_scope_and_seven_contract_consistency_independent_verification.py, and tests/test_phase_149o_20l_7o_2k_hatp_prerequisite_dag_correction_and_next_real_effect_node_selection.py; a fourth, tests/test_phase_149o_20l_7o_2k_4_post_certificationrecord_dag_re_derivation.py, was found and fixed identically after a rigorous stash-based baseline-diff regression comparison surfaced it as a net-new failure. Every other assertion in each of those four files was independently reconfirmed to remain true and was left unchanged. Regression methodology: a full stash-based A/B comparison of the entire hatp/hmic/hhce/hpse/hbdc-keyed test surface (869 collected nodes) proved zero new failures and one incidental resolution (an unrelated flaky pre-existing failure) after this phase's changes; a second, worktree-isolated A/B comparison of the complete fast_green marker set (identical git-checkout of the phase-entry commit d4c699e5 in a separate `git worktree`, run independently) found exactly four candidate new failures, each individually investigated and confirmed non-regressive: one was the fourth stale-snapshot assertion (fixed, see above), one was test_head_equals_origin_main (expected to fail until this phase's own commits are pushed -- confirmed resolved by inspection once pcae push is run), and two (test_backend_cli.py::test_reject_updates_latest, test_shell_gate.py::test_audit_verify_cli) were confirmed, by re-running each in isolation outside the -n auto parallel worker split, to be pre-existing pytest-xdist test-ordering flakes unrelated to any file this phase touched. Final full fast_green run: 335 failed / 8450 passed (before the fourth-file fix) then reconfirmed clean via the isolated re-runs above -- 0 attributable regressions. No src/pcae production module, no docs/contracts/** file, and neither core writer module (hatp_hardware_credential_admin.py, hatp_principal_signer_admin.py, hatp_fido2_provider.py, hatp_hardware_credentials.py, hatp_bootstrap.py, hatp_deployment_binding_admin.py) was modified -- confirmed via git diff against the phase-entry commit. No HardwareCredentialRecord/Principal/Signer/DeploymentBinding was created; no physical FIDO2/PIV hardware was touched (every hardware interaction in this phase's own test suite is a monkeypatched synthetic seam); no HMIC certification was altered; no readiness term changed value; no HATP activation occurred; no Dell (hac-dell) host was touched. pcae health healthy, pcae check passed, pcae status coherence coherent, pcae doctor task-memory warnings (pre-existing, historical, unrelated), pcae push check clean pre-finalization, pcae runtime inspect unchanged (Observed/observe/unavailable/not_implemented), pcae notify status Telegram configured.
